aiSummary: Choctawhatchee Bay is fishing well this week, with recent guide reports confirming a strong speckled trout bite, quality redfish including a 26-lb bull red, and flounder showing up alongside reds and trout on bay charter trips. Today starts calm and sunny with light westerly winds — ideal for an early push — but a 25% chance of afternoon thunderstorms arrives after 1 PM, so plan to be off the water or tucked into protected bayous by early afternoon. The full moon's spring tide is amplifying tidal movement, water temps are holding at 86°F, and slightly stained clarity actually favors reaction bites on darker soft plastics and noisy topwaters through the morning hours.

bridge.aiNote: The 331 Bridge spans the narrow neck of Choctawhatchee Bay, creating a current funnel where bait gets pushed through on both tides. Pilings hold speckled trout, redfish, sheepshead, and black drum year-round, with the lee-side pilings serving as the prime ambush zone on incoming tides. Being open water, this is the first spot to become uncomfortable or unfishable when wind and chop build.
bridge.todaysCall: High tide came through around 5:22 AM, so the outgoing push will be building through the morning — position on the lee-side pilings as current ramps up and bait begins funneling through the bridge neck. Light westerly winds of 0–10 mph should keep chop manageable in the early hours, making this a workable window before midday heat sets in at a heat index near 111°F. The full moon spring tide means stronger-than-average current today, which is a real advantage here; slightly stained water calls for dark-bodied paddle tails or a loud topwater to draw strikes around the pilings. With storms possible after 1 PM and this being an exposed open-water location, target an early start and plan to wrap up by noon.

alaqua.aiNote: Alaqua Bayou offers protected water with a strong year-round redfish population, plus trout and flounder at the mouth. The oyster bars at the creek mouth are the prime fishing zone, and tree cover keeps the bayou a few degrees cooler than the open bay while providing reliable shelter from wind and weather. The upper creek transitions toward brackish water and can hold bass alongside smaller redfish.
alaqua.todaysCall: The outgoing tide running through the afternoon will pull water across the oyster bars at the creek mouth — arrive early while the tide is still dropping and position on those bars to intercept reds and trout moving with the current. Slightly stained water favors darker soft plastics like a root beer or motor oil paddle tail worked slow along the oyster edges. Tree cover here helps cut the brutal heat index today, making it one of the more comfortable spots to fish past mid-morning if you can find shade. With storms threatening after 1 PM, Alaqua's sheltered character makes it a smart choice for stretching your day — but stay weather-aware and have an exit plan.

basin.aiNote: Basin Bayou sees less fishing pressure than nearby Alaqua and LaGrange, meaning fish here tend to be less educated and more willing to commit. The interior grass flats are classic sight-fishing territory for redfish in under two feet of water, and pompano occasionally show at the mouth on moving tides in late spring and early summer. It is somewhat less protected than LaGrange when weather builds.
basin.todaysCall: With light westerly winds forecast this morning, Basin Bayou's interior flats should be fishable — pole or drift the shallow grass quietly and look for redfish tailing or pushing wakes in the slightly stained water. The outgoing tide building through the afternoon will concentrate fish along the edges of the flats and near any defined channels; slightly stained clarity means gold or chartreuse spoons and dark soft plastics will outperform natural colors. The full moon spring tide gives today's outgoing a stronger push than average, which can really fire up the sight-fishing action on shallow flats as bait moves off the grass. Head in before 1 PM — Basin Bayou offers less weather protection than LaGrange if storms develop.

lagrange.aiNote: LaGrange Bayou is considered the top trout producer among the bayous in this area, with legendary oyster bars at the mouth and interior grass flats that hold redfish year-round. Deep holes inside the bayou hold black drum and sheepshead, rounding out a diverse fishery. It is also the most protected water on this side of the bay, making it the reliable go-to when weather builds.
lagrange.todaysCall: Recent guide reports confirm a strong trout bite across the bay, and LaGrange's oyster bars are exactly the kind of structure that concentrates fish during an active bite — work soft plastics or suspending jerkbaits along the bar edges as the outgoing tide builds through mid-morning. The full moon spring tide will amplify the outgoing flow this afternoon, which historically triggers aggressive feeding on the oyster bars; low tide hits around 4:38 PM so the most productive window is the several hours of falling water before that. Slightly stained clarity is no obstacle here — dark-bodied lures or a popping cork with a live shrimp will draw strikes in this water. If afternoon storms do fire up, LaGrange is your safest bet on this side of the bay to wait them out and keep fishing.

fourmile.aiNote: Four Mile Creek is a tidal creek running between Shipyard Marina and the bay, where tidal flow pushes baitfish up the creek on incoming tides and concentrates redfish and trout in the bends and grass edges. The creek mouth is a prime flounder zone, and the upper section transitions toward brackish water that can hold bass alongside smaller redfish. Short and heavily sheltered, it is the safest fishery in the area when weather threatens.
fourmile.todaysCall: Today's outgoing tide is the dominant afternoon movement, so focus on the bends and grass edges inside the creek as bait gets pulled back toward the bay — reds and trout will stack in these ambush spots. The creek mouth is worth working for flounder on the outgoing flow; slightly stained water calls for a chartreuse or white grub bounced slowly along the bottom near the mouth. With Four Mile being short and protected, it's an excellent option for fishing through the heat of the day when the heat index approaches 111°F, and it's the smartest place to be if afternoon storms develop ahead of schedule. Given its proximity to Shipyard Marina, it's also an easy bail-out — you can be off the water in minutes if lightning threatens.

hogtown.aiNote: Hogtown Bayou is a signature Santa Rosa Beach guide destination and one of the most consistently productive trout flats on Choctawhatchee Bay. Summer mornings are the peak window, with trout stacking on grass flats in two to four feet of water. Spanish mackerel show at the mouth on moving tides, and while the bayou sees regular guide pressure it continues to produce reliably.
hogtown.todaysCall: This is the spot most directly supported by recent reports — Santa Rosa Beach guides have been hammering speckled trout in this area, and Hogtown is exactly the kind of grass-flat fishery those reports are describing. Hit it early: summer mornings are the proven peak window here, and with light westerly winds you should have glassy or near-glassy conditions on the flat at first light. Work dark soft plastics or a popping cork over grass in two to four feet as the outgoing tide builds, and check the mouth for Spanish mackerel on any moving current. Factor in your run time from the 331 Bridge, and be headed back before 1 PM given the storm window — this is not the place to get caught in afternoon lightning.

rocky.aiNote: Rocky Bayou sits inside Fred Gannon Rocky Bayou State Park near Niceville, offering protected, scenic water that sees significantly less pressure than bayous closer to the 331 Bridge. Freshwater influence from Rocky Creek makes flounder fishing excellent, and the glass-calm state park coves are ideal for sight-fishing redfish. Mangrove snapper hold near dock pilings, and it is the furthest location from Shipyard Marina — run time is a real consideration.
rocky.todaysCall: Light westerly winds this morning mean the run to Rocky Bayou should be comfortable, but factor your transit time carefully given the afternoon storm window — you want to be fishing, not running, when 1 PM arrives. The freshwater influence here slightly offsets the 86°F bay temps, and the calm state park coves are perfect for sight-fishing reds in slightly stained water; a gold weedless spoon or a dark soft plastic on a light jig head are ideal. Work dock pilings for mangrove snapper on a small jig or live shrimp — these fish don't care about tide stage and are a reliable bonus target. The full moon spring tide will move water through the bayou more aggressively than usual today, so watch for flounder staging near the creek mouth and any defined drop-offs on the falling tide.

mack.aiNote: Mack Bayou sits on the barrier-island, 30-A side of Choctawhatchee Bay near Topsail Hill Preserve State Park, well west of the 331 Bridge — a genuine long-run destination rather than a quick local trip. It shares the classic protected-bayou character of Alaqua and LaGrange, with marsh grass, oyster bars, and a few interior holes, and sees less pressure simply due to its distance from the main boat ramps. Hewett Bayou and Buck Bayou lie immediately to the east and are realistically fishable in the same trip.
mack.todaysCall: If you're making the run to the 30-A side today, leave at first light — you need fishing time banked before the post-1 PM storm window, and this is a long run from Shipyard Marina. Light westerly winds this morning should give you a manageable crossing; once inside, work oyster bars and marsh grass edges on the outgoing tide with dark soft plastics or gold spoons for reds and trout. The full moon spring tide means a stronger-than-average outgoing pull this afternoon, which tends to concentrate fish along defined edges in bayous like this one. Combine the trip with Hewett and Buck to make the run worthwhile, and watch the western sky closely — build in plenty of time to get back across open water before storms fire.

hewett.aiNote: Hewett Bayou sits immediately east of Mack Bayou on the barrier-island, 30-A side of Choctawhatchee Bay near Topsail Hill Preserve State Park, making it a natural partner to Mack and Buck Bayou in a single long-run trip. It offers the same protected-bayou habitat — oyster bars and marsh grass at the mouth, a few deeper interior holes — and sees light pressure thanks to its distance from the main boat ramps.
hewett.todaysCall: Pair Hewett with Mack Bayou on the same trip and leave early to maximize time before the afternoon storm threat. The outgoing tide building through mid-morning will activate the oyster bar and marsh grass edges at the mouth — work dark paddle tails or a popping cork through those zones for trout and reds in slightly stained water. Interior holes are worth probing for any fish that have pushed deeper ahead of the falling tide as water clarity stains up slightly. Keep the same weather discipline as Mack: the 30-A side crossing requires open-water running, so be headed home well before 1 PM.

buck.aiNote: Buck Bayou is the smallest and least-documented of the three neighboring bayous on the barrier-island, 30-A side of Choctawhatchee Bay near Topsail Hill Preserve State Park. Its habitat should track its larger neighbors — marsh grass, some oyster structure, and a modest interior — though there is less basis to speak confidently about its specific fishing characteristics. It is best approached as a bonus stop on a Mack and Hewett Bayou trip rather than a standalone destination.
buck.todaysCall: Treat Buck Bayou as a quick bonus stop while you're already on the 30-A side fishing Mack and Hewett — poke in, work the mouth structure and any visible oyster edges on the outgoing tide, and move on if it doesn't produce quickly. Slightly stained water means you're relying on lure action and presentation over sight-fishing precision; a dark soft plastic or small gold spoon covering water efficiently is the right call. Given the limited documentation on this spot, don't burn precious morning time here at the expense of the more proven neighboring bayous. As with all the 30-A locations today, the 1 PM storm window means your departure timeline from this side of the bay is non-negotiable.
